body:
> The same error occurs on all queries intermittently.

This is odd. This error indicates data corruption, which should not be intermittent. Can you narrow it down to one series/query/time range?

2.15.0 did change a lot about how we read the index, however that error comes from a chunk.

Is there an easy way to isolate this from grafana? Basically what I see is that I have a big dashboard and if it set the query time to high (6h or so) some of the panels error out for a few seconds then come back. I'll investigate some more as well and can probably share the dashboard with you directly if needed
Also I upgraded from 2.12 to 2.15 with the same volume to store the data, so it's ready data written by the older Prometheus I assume? which may be why the time matters
The data format on disk has not changed.

> This is odd. This error indicates data corruption, which should not be intermittent. Can you narrow it down to one series/query/time range?

@brian-brazil No I cannot narrow it down to a specific series or time or date.  For example I have a dashboard that tracks the outgoing traffic for a CDN I help run and retrying the query fixes this problem.  Reloading the same dashboard will make different panels break.

The Prometheus 2.0 Dashboard that Grafana creates also exhibits this behavior for me retrying fixes it.  The only thing I seem to notice is shorter time spans (last 15) can usually work however going to an hour timespan can break.

Most of the series in question do have a high Cardinality could that be related?
I experienced the same issue straight after upgrading to 2.15.0 both in a kubernetes pod and a stand-alone prometheus server on Fedora 31. No other changes except for the prometheus upgrade.
I just downgraded to version 2.14.0 and the problem has gone away. Definitely caused by 2.15.0
@damm regarding the cardinality: I do have a super small prometheues instance with ~1.3k series, highest cardinality labels at 405 and highest cardinality metrics at 130, but see the same behavior.
While @brian-brazil is right that on-disk format has not changed, it is the first release where we verify checksums.
Can we know if you repeat an errorful API query if you get the error repeatedly? If grafana refreshes then the query is probably shifted in time.

I get the feeling there is a problem with concurrency.

I have the following two loops:
```
for TIME in {1577173160..1577174660}; do curl "http://localhost:9090/api/v1/query?query=sum(increase(gateway_wan_bytes_received%5B30d%5D))&start=${TIME}&end=$((TIME+300))&step=15"; done;
```
```
for TIME in {1577173500..1577174000}; do curl "http://localhost:9090/api/v1/query?query=sum(increase(gateway_wan_bytes_sent%5B5y%5D))%2F(sum(increase(gateway_wan_bytes_received%5B5y%5D))%2Bsum(increase(gateway_wan_bytes_sent%5B5y%5D)))&start=${TIME}&end=$((TIME+300))&step=15"; done;
```

Both loops run through multiple times without any error if I ran only one at a time.
As soon as I started to run both parallel, I got the checksum mismatch errors.

EDIT: a concurrency problem also match an other observation of mine.
Bigger grafana dashboards, with more panels and therefore more concurrent requests, are more often affected than smaller dashboards.
I was also seeing this on one of my instances, downgrading from 2.15.0 to 2.14.0 fixes it.

we're facing the exact same issues with this version
2.14.0 works just fine

> it is the first release where we verify checksums.

Ah, #6040. That's data corruption being correctly detected then.
I would like to understand why so many people are affected and why it 'resolves' itself.
Hmm, the crc32 object is shared between calls to Chunk. Is that called concurrently?

issue.title: tsdb: Do not reuse the same crc32 hash between Chunk() calls

repository.name: prometheus
repository.description: The Prometheus monitoring system and time series database.

issue.body:
The same crc32 object was called concurrently between chunks. As this
object is only used in that function, create a new one each time the
function is run.

See #6512

Signed-off-by: Julien Pivotto <roidelapluie@inuits.eu>

Yup, we have race on `s.crc32` and `s.buf` on chunk file reader. https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/6514 fixed most of it, s.buf is still to remove (: 

@roidelapluie are you on it? Can take it over. We might need patch release for this.
